result.title: Decoder-as-a-Probe: Verbalizing and Steering Visual Representations in LVLMs
result.summary: It is commonly accepted that high-level concepts are represented linearly in the representation space of large neural networks. For Large Vision Language Models (LVLMs), finding those interpretable directions in visual representations is important for interpretability. To find them, the classical approach is to train a linear classifier on the representations, but it needs a large amount of labels and only recovers what can be read from the representations, not what the model actually uses. In this paper we start from the following insight: The LLM Decoder of an LVLM is also a classifier whose classes are the possible next tokens. So we use its first-order Taylor expansion as a linear classifier. Hence, we introduce Decoder-as-a-Probe (DaP), which significantly outperforms classical probing and steering baselines especially when training data is sparse. (1) It verbalizes what an LVLM perceives in a given image. (2) It can surgically change the perception of the LVLM about specific attributes (e.g. change only the color, the clothes worn or the action done). Due to its simplicity and data efficiency, we believe DaP can serve as a plug-and-play tool for LVLM research, such as interpretability, hallucination mitigation or instruction tuning.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Decoder-as-a-Probe（DaP），将 LVLM 的 LLM 解码器的一阶泰勒展开当作线性分类器，从视觉表示中读出模型感知的图像内容，并能定向修改颜色、服饰、动作等特定属性的感知，在标注稀疏时优于传统 probing 与 steering 基线。
AI.relevance_reason: 它区分「表示中可读出」与「模型实际使用」，为核查视觉细节是否保留在内部状态、答案是否真正依赖视觉证据提供了低成本探针，与 LVR 的视觉证据筛选兴趣有具体联系，但未涉及 latent 推理轨迹或多步状态更新，需读原文确认其因果性主张。
